## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Sālūkajātaka* (Ja 286) is a birth story belonging to the Jātaka collection of the Pali Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. According to its opening frame, the Buddha delivered the tale while residing at Jetavana concerning a monk who was tempted by a "fat girl" (*thullakumārikā*), an occasion cross-referenced to the narrative background of the *Cullanāradakassapajātaka* [SuttaCentral]. In the story's verse opening ("Envy not what Celery eats"), the focal character Celery (Sālūka) is a pig fattened up for a feast [SuttaCentral]. In the concluding identification (*samodhāna*), the Buddha identifies the characters: the fat maiden of the past was the fat maiden of the present, the pig Sālūka was the lovesick or dissatisfied monk (*ukkaṇṭhitabhikkhu*), Cullalohita was Ānanda, and Mahālohita was the Bodhisatta himself [Fausböll 1879]. Following the exposition of the truths, the monk is recorded to have attained the fruit of stream-entry (*sotāpattiphala*) [Fausböll 1879].
Neither SuttaCentral nor DharmaNexus identifies cross-language parallels in Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan corpora [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. SuttaCentral records four modern translations of the text in four languages [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus detects Pali-internal text reuse across three matches (307 characters) with the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (Dutiyo bhāgo), the longest continuous match aligning verses §1.1–2.4 with commentary sections §2690–2694 at a similarity of 0.94 [DharmaNexus].
